claims.claim: **Open globe = the cornea or sclera is injured through its full thickness**, from rupture (usually blunt) or laceration (sharp object or high-velocity projectile). **It is a serious threat to vision.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Penetrating eye injury' (Last updated October 2022), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Penetrating_eye_injury/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Look for it alongside serious head injury or multiple trauma.** Ask about mechanism and the composition of any possible intraocular foreign body (soil, dirt, metal).
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Penetrating eye injury' (Last updated October 2022), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Penetrating_eye_injury/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Signs of perforation:** protruding missile (**leave it alone — don't touch or remove it**) · loss of red reflex · severe loss of vision · RAPD · squashed or distorted globe · swollen haemorrhagic lids · chemosis · distorted, irregular or peaked pupil · **360 degree subconjunctival haemorrhage** · extruding ocular contents · altered anterior chamber depth.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Penetrating eye injury' (Last updated October 2022), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Penetrating_eye_injury/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **A cursory examination may be enough**, but attempt visual acuity and check for a relative afferent pupillary defect.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Penetrating eye injury' (Last updated October 2022), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Penetrating_eye_injury/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Avoid any pressure on the globe** — through examination or padding — because eye contents may be extruded. **Do not force the eyelids open.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Penetrating eye injury' (Last updated October 2022), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Penetrating_eye_injury/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **In young children with a highly suggestive mechanism, an ophthalmologist examines under procedural sedation or GA.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Penetrating eye injury' (Last updated October 2022), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Penetrating_eye_injury/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Urgently notify ophthalmology, place an eye shield and keep the child fasted from first contact.** Do not remove a protruding foreign body.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Penetrating eye injury' (Last updated October 2022), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Penetrating_eye_injury/, retrieved 2026-09-23

The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Penetrating eye injury' (Last updated October 2022), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Penetrating_eye_injury/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Analgesia — consider NSAIDs — plus an antiemetic such as ondansetron**, because vomiting raises intraocular pressure and can expel ocular contents.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Penetrating eye injury' (Last updated October 2022), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Penetrating_eye_injury/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Bed rest with the head of the bed at 30 degrees** if haemodynamically able. **Check tetanus status.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Penetrating eye injury' (Last updated October 2022), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Penetrating_eye_injury/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Prophylaxis, no signs of infection:** oral ciprofloxacin 20 mg/kg (max 750 mg) twice daily.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Penetrating eye injury' (Last updated October 2022), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Penetrating_eye_injury/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Suspected endophthalmitis or signs of infection:** IV ceftazidime 50 mg/kg (max 2 g) 8-hourly **and** vancomycin 15 mg/kg (max 750 mg) 6-hourly.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Penetrating eye injury' (Last updated October 2022), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Penetrating_eye_injury/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Image the orbit (X-ray or CT) after discussion with ophthalmology** when an intraocular foreign body is suspected.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Penetrating eye injury' (Last updated October 2022), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Penetrating_eye_injury/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Involve the paediatric team if child abuse is suspected; transfer** if open-globe management is beyond local capability.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Penetrating eye injury' (Last updated October 2022), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Penetrating_eye_injury/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Discharge when** an open-globe injury has been excluded or dealt with **and** the child is symptom-free or has a clear follow-up plan with early-review criteria.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Penetrating eye injury' (Last updated October 2022), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Penetrating_eye_injury/, retrieved 2026-09-23
